An alternate method is by calculating the risk period i.e., 3 days before and 3 days after ovulation. Ovulation can also be estimated by changes in cervical mucus and basal body temperature.
[[IMG:3]]
[[IMG:4]]
Another method of calculating the safe period is the Knaus–Ogino method. The fertile period is determined by subtracting 18 days from the shortest cycle and 10 days from the longest cycle. This gives the first and the last day of the fertile period, respectively.

questions.stem: What does Billing's method of contraception refer to?
questions.explanation:
Billing’s method of contraception refers to the cervical mucus method. It is also called ovulation method.
The properties of the cervical mucus change during the menstrual cycle. The female partner can predict the fertile period by examining her cervical mucus.
Under the influence of estrogen, the mucus increases in quantity and becomes more slippery and elastic i.e. wet days. This continues till it reaches a peak. After this, under the influence of progesterone, it becomes thicker, scanty i.e. dry days.
Abstinence is advised during the wet days till 4 days after the peak day. The safe period includes the dry days after menses till the appearance of mucus and from the 4th day after the peak day.
The pattern of cervical mucus secretion during a menstrual cycle is given below.

questions.stem: Identify the contraceptive shown in the given image.
questions.explanation:
The given image shows a female condom. It consists of a pouch made of polyurethane which is 17 cm in length with a flexible ring at each end. The inner ring at the closed end is smaller than the outer ring.
The inner ring is inserted at the apex of the vagina and the outer ring remains outside. It covers the cervix, the entire vagina, and external genitalia. Hence, it provides protection against HIV and STDs. It has a failure rate of 5–15 per 100 woman-years, which is higher than that of a male condom.
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
It can be fitted by the patient hours before intercourse, and easily removed soon after. It covers the cervix, vagina, and external genitalia and is protective against sexually transmitted diseases. It can also be worn in the puerperal period, unlike the cervical diaphragm.
The female condom should not be used along with a male condom because if worn together they may slip, tear, or become displaced.
The given image below shows the insertion of a female condom:

questions.stem: A nulliparous woman has been using Today sponge as a contraceptive. What does this contain? [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]]
questions.explanation:
Today sponge contains 1 g of nonoxynol 9. It is a mushroom-shaped polyurethane disposable sponge that is 2 inches wide and 1.25 inches thick.
It is provided with a loop for easy removal. It should be placed high up in the vagina with the concave side covering the cervix. It can remain effective for 24 h. It can be used only once.
It acts as a mechanical barrier preventing the entry of sperms into the cervical canal, absorbs semen, and contains a spermicidal agent. The failure rate is 9-16 per 100 woman-years.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a contraindication for the use of the contraceptive shown below?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
The given image shows a cervical diaphragm or Dutch cap. It can be used by women having multiple sex partners.
Contraindications of cervical diaphragm usage:
Prolapse, cystocele, rectocele - accurate fitting is not possible
Recurrent urinary tract infection
Allergy to rubber or spermicidal agent
It must be removed following intercourse as it can lead to toxic shock syndrome (TSS) if left in the vagina for a long period. TSS is caused by Streptococcus pyogenes or Staphylococcus
aureus infection.

questions.stem: You are prescribing nonoxynol-9 jelly to a woman using a cervical diaphragm for contraception. What is its mechanism of action? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
Nonoxynol-9 is one of the spermicidal agents which act by disruption of the sperm cell membrane.
Spermicidal agents are chemical contraceptives as they contain surfactants, such as nonoxynol-9, octoxynol, menfegol and enzyme-inhibiting agents. These are available as:
Foam tablets
Soluble pessaries
Creams
Jellies
Films
The spermicidal agent remains effective for 1–2 hours after the application. They are always used along with other contraceptives such as the diaphragm, cervical cap, and condom. When they are used alone, the failure rate is high i.e., 30 per 100 woman-years.
Chronic use of spermicides can cause vaginal irritation, abrasion, and ulceration. This increases the risk of HIV spread. Hence, spermicidal agents should not be recommended to HIV-positive couples.

questions.stem: A young woman who is using a cervical diaphragm asks for an alternative contraceptive. You suggest a recently launched contraceptive Phexxi. What is its composition?
options: Lactic acid, Citric Acid, Potassium bitartrate
Ascorbic acid, Citric acid, Calcium bitartrate
Lactic acid, Ascorbic acid, Potassium bitartrate
Ascorbic acid, Lactic acid, Calcium bitartrate.
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
Phexxi is a vaginal gel that contains lactic acid, citric acid, and potassium bitartrate.
Phexxi is a vaginal pH regulator which is a non-hormonal contraceptive. It works by maintaining vaginal pH within the range of 3.5 to 4.5. This acidic environment is inhospitable for sperms.
Phexxi comes in pre-filled vaginal applicators. A single dose must be applied before vaginal intercourse. If more than one act of vaginal intercourse occurs within one hour, an additional dose must be applied.

questions.stem: A newly married woman was prescribed Mala-N at a PHC. What is its composition?
questions.explanation:
Mala-N is a combined oral contraceptive containing 0.15 mg levonorgestrel (LNG) and 0.03 mg ethinyl estradiol. It is supplied free of cost through all PHC's, urban family welfare centers, etc.
All combined oral pills contain a mixture of ethinyl estradiol in a dose of 20-30 mcg and an orally active progestogen. Mala-D has the same composition as Mala-N but is available at a price of Rs 3/- per packet.
Combined oral pill works by suppressing pituitary hormones, FSH, and LH peak which prevents ovulation. At the same time, progestogen causes atrophic changes in the endometrium and
prevents implantation.
Progestogen also acts on the cervical mucus making it thick and tenacious and impenetrable by sperms. It also interferes with tubal motility and alters tubal transport.
, so the fertilized egg reaches the uterine cavity before the endometrium is receptive for implantation.
These tablets are taken starting on the first day of the cycle for 21 days. A new course of tablets should be commenced 7 days after the cessation of the previous course. They should be taken at bedtime, preferably after a meal.
[[IMG:1]]

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an advantage of norgestimate OCPs?
questions.explanation:
Norgestimate is one of the 3rd generation progesterone agents. All OCPs have the disadvantage of increasing the risk of venous thrombosis.
Third-generation progesterone agents are less androgenic and so reduce the occurrence of acne and hirsutism. They also have a lower risk of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders compared to the previous generation progesterone agents.
Benefits of combined pills:
Effective contraceptive
Useful in menorrhagia and polymenorrhoea
Relieves dysmenorrhoea and premenstrual tension
Prevents anaemia by reducing the menstrual loss
Lower incidence of benign breast neoplasia (fibrocystic disease), functional ovarian cyst, ovarian and uterine malignancy
Reduced risk of PID - due to thick cervical mucus caused by progestogen, preventing the organisms from entering into the uterine cavity
Reduced incidence of ectopic pregnancy - due to suppression of ovulation and decreased risk of PID
Protects against rheumatoid arthritis
Reduces the risk of anorectal cancer
Useful in acne, PCOD, and endometriosis

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a contraindication to the use of OCPs? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
Thyroid disorders like hypothyroidism are not a contraindication for OCP usage. Contraindications of OCPs:
Absolute contraindications -
Breast and genital cancers
Liver disease
History of thromboembolism
Cardiac abnormalities
Congenital hyperlipidemia
Undiagnosed abnormal uterine bleeding
Relative contraindications -
Age over 40 years, if smoker >35 years
Mild hypertension
[[IMG:2]]
Chronic renal disease
Epilepsy
Migraine
First 6 months of breastfeeding
Diabetes mellitus
Gallbladder disease
History of infrequent bleeding or amenorrhea

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs do not lead to failure of OCPs?
questions.explanation:
Sodium valproate is an inhibitor of CYP enzymes that are responsible for OCP metabolism. Thus, it does not lead to OCP failure.
Drugs leading to OCP failure are :
Rifampicin
Tetracyclines - interferes with enterohepatic circulation of estrogen
Phenytoin
Phenobarbitone
Antifungals
Cephalosporin
Ritonavir for HIV - interferes with absorption of OCP
Most of the anti-convulsants are enzyme inducers and hence increase the clearance of OCPs. This leads to OCP failure.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not the mechanism of action of progesterone only pills?
options: Kills the sperms in the cervical canal
questions.explanation:
Minipills or progesterone-only pills (POP) do not kill sperm in the cervical canal. Progesterone-only pills act by thickening the cervical mucus (the main mechanism of all POPs
except cerazette) that inhibits penetration of sperms, inhibiting tubal motility, and suppressing ovulation.
Other advantages of POPs include a reduction in the incidence of pelvic inflammatory diseases and sexually transmitted diseases (due to thickened cervical mucus).
Due to the inhibition of tubal motility, the absolute risk of all pregnancies including ectopic pregnancy decreases, while the relative risk of ectopic pregnancy increases. But a previous history of ectopic pregnancy is not a contraindication for POP.
POPs do not affect clotting, lipid metabolism, and carbohydrate metabolism. So they can safely be used by women who are obese, breastfeeding, hypertensive, have SLE or a history of thromboembolism, diabetic with vascular disease. Significant adverse effects of POPs are irregular bleeding (mostly scanty), and secondary amenorrhea after longtime usage as it causes endometrial atrophy.
[[IMG:1]]
Contraindications for POPs include undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, pregnancy, known or suspected breast cancer, and benign or malignant liver tumors.

questions.stem: A patient has come to your clinic for contraceptive advice. As she has a family history of breast cancer, you suggest a non-hormonal oral contraceptive to her. What is the initial dose of this drug?
questions.explanation:
Centchroman is a non-hormonal oral contraceptive that is started at a dose of 30 mg on the first day of the menstrual cycle. It can be given to women with a family history of breast cancer where hormonal contraceptives are contraindicated.
Centchroman or ormeloxifene is a synthetic nonsteroidal contraceptive. Following the initial dose of 30 mg on the first day of menses, it is taken twice weekly for 12 weeks and weekly thereafter. It prevents implantation through endometrial changes. The return of fertility occurs within 6 months of stopping the drug.
It can also be used as a postcoital pill, given in 60 mg dose within 24 hours of coitus. It has a failure rate of 1.83 per 100 woman years. It does not provide protection against HIV and other STDs.
Side effects of centchroman:
Headache, nausea, vomiting
Weight gain
Delay in return of fertility (up to 6 months)
Atypical endometrial hyperplasia - prolonged use Contraindications of centchroman:
PCOD
Hepatic dysfunction
Cervical dysplasia
Allergy to the drug
This drug has been developed by Central Drug Research Institute, Lucknow. It has been released in India under the name of Chhaya (previously called Saheli) under the National Family Planning
Programme.

[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
[[IMG:3]]

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most effective reversible method of contraception? [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]]
questions.explanation:
The most effective reversible method of contraception among the given options is Norplant, which is a subdermal hormonal implant.
The most effective method of contraception overall is sterilization, which is one of the permament methods. Both methods belong to the first-tier category of contraceptives.
There are 2 types of subdermal implants:
Implanon (which has replaced Norplant I)
Norplant II
The implants work by inhibition of ovulation, endometrial atrophy, and thickening of cervical mucus. Implanon contains desogestrel and also reduces acne and osteoporosis.
The implants are inserted on the first day of the menstrual cycle, within 5 days of abortion, and 3 weeks after the delivery. The woman needs to use barrier contraception or abstain in the first 7 days of insertion.
The image below shows an implanon:
686	Sold by @itachibot
The image given below shows the insertion of a subdermal implant:
[[IMG:3]]
[[IMG:4]]
[[IMG:5]]
Advantages of implants:
Long-acting with sustained effect
Good compliance
Coital-independent with no nuisance of daily oral or frequent injections
Failure rate - 0.2 and 1.3 per 100 woman-years
Implanon reduces acne and osteoporosis. Disadvantages of implants:
Breakthrough bleeding
Irregular cycles
Amenorrhoea
Ectopic pregnancy
Local infection
Requires insertion and removal with nonbiodegradable capsules
Expensive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a mechanism of action of the device given in the image below?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
The given image shows Multiload Cu250, which is one of the copper containing IUCDs. Formation of cervical mucus plug is not one of its mechanisms of action. However, progesterone-containing IUCDs can alter the cervical mucus along with the local effects.
The various mechanisms of action of a copper-containing IUCD are:
Interference with the migration of spermatozoa
Foreign body reaction releasing prostaglandins - provokes uterine contractility and increases the tubal peristalsis which interferes with implantation
Leucocytic infiltration in the endometrium - macrophages engulf the fertilized egg if it enters the endometrial tissue
Enzymatic and metabolic changes in the endometrial tissue which interferes with implantation of the fertilized ovum
Some IUCDs like CuT-380A are effective for up to 10 years.
They are a good choice of method of contraception for the following groups of women:
Having low risk of STD
Multiparous woman
Having a monogamous relationship
Wanting long-term reversible method of contraception
Unreliable users of oral contraception or barrier contraception
IUCDs are avoided in unmarried and nulliparous patients because of the risk of PID and subsequent tubal infertility. Copper IUCDs can also be used as emergency contraception following intercourse.

questions.stem: IUCD insertion is being considered in a multiparous woman who wants long-term contraception. This method of contraception is absolutely contraindicated in all of the following except . [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
IUCDs can be used in HIV-affected women.
Intrauterine contraceptive devices (IUCDs) provide long-term contraception by preventing fertilization.
Contraindications for IUCD insertion:
Suspected pregnancy
Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)
Lower genital tract infection
Presence of fibroids
Severe anaemia
Uncontrolled diabetes - due to increased pelvic infection
Scarred uterus eg, post caesarean section
Septate uterus
[[IMG:2]]
Menorrhagia and dysmenorrhoea - if Copper T is used
Breast cancer - if LNG IUCD is used Complications of IUCD usage:
Immediate -
Vasovagal attack
Uterine cramps
Early -
Expulsion of IUCD
Perforation of uterus
Spotting, menorrhagia
Dysmenorrhoea
Vaginal infection
Actinomycosis
Late -
PID
Ectopic pregnancy
Perforation of uterus
Menorrhagia
Dysmenorrhoea
The failure rate of IUCD is 1–3 per 100 woman-years.
Levonorgestrel IUCD also causes hormonal adverse effects such as headache, acne, breast tenderness, and functional ovarian cysts. Amenorrhoea occurs in 35% of women after 2 years of use.

questions.stem: You are inserting Nova-T in a patient for spacing of births. This device contains .
questions.explanation:
Nova-T contains both copper and silver. The addition of the silver increases its effective lifespan.
In copper-carrying devices, copper wire is wrapped around the vertical stem of a polypropylene frame. Some of them have copper wire wrapped around the arms too. Based on the surface area, they are of various types:
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
Copper T 380 A
Multiload copper 250
Copper T 200
Copper 7
Copper T 220
Nova-T
They are effective for 3–5 years. It is estimated that about 50 mcg of copper is eluted daily in the uterus. Copper T 380A, known as Paraguard, has a lifespan of 10 years. Nova T has a lifespan of 5 years.

questions.stem: A nursing mother was prescribed progestasert for contraception. How much progesterone is released by this device?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
Progestasert releases 65 g of progesterone/day.
Progestasert is a T-shaped device carrying 38 mg of progesterone in a silicon oil reservoir in the vertical stem. The progesterone released causes the formation of a thick plug of mucus at the cervical os. This prevents entry of the sperms in addition to the local contraceptive effect of IUCDs.
There is lesser incidence of menstrual problems like menorrhagia and dysmenorrhoea compared to copper-containing intrauterine devices. However, it is expensive and requires yearly replacement.

questions.stem: Which of the following increases the risk of pelvic inflammatory disease?
questions.explanation:
Copper IUCDs increase the risk of PID.
OCPs, Mirena and DMPA injectables contain progesterone which causes thickening of the cervical mucus and decreases the motility of the female genital tract. Thus, they reduce the risk of PID by preventing the ascent of bacteria from the vagina.

questions.stem: What is the most effective mode of contraception for a woman with heart disease? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
IUCDs are the most effective mode of contraception for women with heart diseases. IUCDs are safe in these patients and come under the first-tier contraceptive methods.
Condoms are not contraindicated in heart disease patients but they are third-tier contraceptives. Hence, they are not as effective as IUCDs.
OCPs and hormonal implants are contraindicated in patients with heart diseases as the constituent hormones can cause thromboembolic disorders.

questions.stem: Which of the following techniques of permanent contraception does not require an abdominal incision?
questions.explanation:
Essure permanent device is a method of hysteroscopic sterilization. Pomeroy, Parkland, and Irving procedures are methods for tubal ligation via an abdominal approach.
Essure device consists of a micro-inserter with a flexible inner coil made of stainless steel and a dynamic outer coil made of nickel titanium alloy (nitinol).
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
This device is inserted into the fallopian tube by hysteroscopy. It acts by benign local fibrous tissue growth leading to occlusion of the tube. The failure rate is 3.5%.
Its advantages are that there is no abdominal scar and the procedure can be done under local anaesthesia.
Disadvantages of Essure:
Hysteroscopy required for the procedure and to confirm the blockage
Expensive procedure
Expertise required
Irreversible - tuboplasty for reversal not possible
3 months waiting time to ensure sterility - HSG must be done after 3 months to confirm tubal blockage
Bilateral insertion difficult due to spasm
Can cause perforation of the tube

questions.stem: A woman has come to your clinic for a checkup following tubal ligation by Pomeroy technique. Which portion of the tube is ligated in this technique?
questions.explanation:
Isthmus of the fallopian tube is ligated in Pomeroy technique. It is the most popular technique of tubal ligation.
Midline, paramedian or transverse abdominal incision is made 2 inches above the pubic symphysis (1 inch in puerperal sterilisation). The fallopian tube is identified, made into a loop and tied at the base. The loop is then excised.
The operation is simple and requires a short period of hospitalization. The failure rate is only 0.4% and it is mainly due to spontaneous canalization. It is surgically reversible.
The below image shows Pomeroy’s method of tubal ligation.
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]

questions.stem: Fimbriectomy is also known as:
questions.explanation:
Fimbriectomy is also known as Kroener's procedure. This procedure involves ligation of the distal ampulla of the tube with two permanent sutures. Then, resection of the infundibulum of the tube is done.
Some more techniques of permanent sterilization include:
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
[[IMG:3]]
Pomeroy method - The fallopian tube is identified on each side, brought out through the incision. The middle portion is formed into a loop which is tied at the base with catgut and excised. This is the most commonly used technique.
Uchida's method - The tubal serosa is stripped off the muscular layer in the midsegment of the tube. The muscle layer is excised. The proximal end is ligated and buried in the broad ligament. This minimal excision of the tube preserves the potential for tuboplasty.
Irving's procedure - The mid-portion of the tube is ligated and the intervening portion is excised. The proximal end is buried in the myometrium and the distal end is buried in the broad ligament. It is a reliable method but irreversible and may require a laparotomy incision.
[[IMG:4]]
[[IMG:5]]
[[IMG:6]]
Madlener's procedure - A loop of the fallopian tube is crushed and then ligated with a nonabsorbable suture.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old male patient underwent a vasectomy. What is the failure rate of this procedure? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:2]]
[[IMG:3]]
The failure rate of vasectomy is 0.15%
This procedure is done under local anaesthesia. A small incision is made in the scrotum. The vas deferens are divided on both sides which disrupts the passage of sperms.
The no-scalpel technique has been now adopted. One single incision is made with special forceps and skin stitch is not required. Clips and plugs can be applied over the vas instead of cutting.
The sperms can remain in the reproductive tract for up to 3 months. Hence, sterility is not immediate. The couple must abstain from intercourse during this period or use other methods of contraception.
Approximately, 20 ejaculates clear the semen of all sperms. Two semen analysis reports must confirm the absence of sperms before the man can be declared sterile.
[[IMG:4]]

questions.stem: A couple with a history of unprotected sexual intercourse requires emergency contraception. Which of the following is not a mechanism by which these drugs act?
options: Preventing the implantation of the fertilized egg
questions.explanation:
Emergency contraceptives do not interrupt early pregnancy, once conception has occured. They are used to prevent pregnancy after unprotected intercourse. Hence, they are also
called interceptives.
The main action of emergency contraceptives is to make the endometrium unsuitable for implantation. They can also delay or inhibit ovulation, and prevent fertilization of the egg by sperms.
[[IMG:1]]
Methods of emergency contraception:
Drug | Dose
Levonorgestrel | 0.75mg stat and repeat dose after 12 hours or1.5mg as a si ngle dose
Ethinyl estradiol 50 g + Nor gestrel 0.25 mg | 2 tabs stat and 2 tabs after 12 hours
RU486 (Mifepristone) | Single dose of 25-50mg
Ethinyl Estradiol | 2.5 mg BD X 5 days
Copper IUDs | Insertion within 5 days of int ercourse
Centchroman | 2 tabs(60 mg) to be taken twi ce at an interval of 12 hoursS hould be taken within 24 hou rs of intercourse.
Ulipristal | 30 mg within 5 days of interc ourse

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman comes to the clinic with a history of unprotected intercourse 2 days ago. Which of the following will you prescribe as a single dose contraceptive?
questions.explanation:
Levonorgestrel (LNG) 1.5 mg i.e. 2 tablets of LNG 0.75 mg can be used as a single dose emergency contraceptive. This should be taken within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse.
Alternatively, one tablet of LNG 0.75mg can be followed by another tablet 12 hours later. The tablets can be offered up to 120 hours but the efficacy decreases with the increase in interval between coitus and drug intake.
LNG prevents ovulation and makes endometrium unsuitable for implantation. The failure rate is 1.1%. If pregnancy occurs as a result of contraceptive failure, the risk of ectopic pregnancy increases but it is not teratogenic.
Advantages of LNG:
No oestrogen and its associated side effects
Can be used in hypertensive, cardiac and diabetic patients
Suitable for lactating woman
Can be given up to 120 hours after the unprotected intercourse
Single-dose therapy Contraindications of LNG:
Liver disease
Thrombophlebitis
Migraine
[[IMG:1]]
Galactose allergy - as the tablet contains lactose

questions.stem: What is the dose of ulipristal for emergency contraception?
questions.explanation:
The dose of ulipristal is 30 mg tablet and it should be taken within 5 days of intercourse.
Ulipristal is a synthetic progesterone receptor modulator. It attaches to the progesterone receptor and acts by:
Preventing/delaying ovulation
Suppressing endometrial and follicular growth
Inhibiting implantation
Side effects are headaches and mood changes. It is contraindicated in women with severe hepatic dysfunction and severe asthma.
Note: The use of ulipristal for the treatment of fibroids has been discontinued due to the increased incidence of severe liver injury.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a risk factor for bacterial vaginosis? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
Caucasian race is not a risk factor for bacterial vaginosis. The risk factors for bacterial vaginosis are:
Oral sex
Vaginal douching
African race
Cigarette smoking
Sex during menses
Intrauterine device
Early age of sexual intercourse
New or multiple sexual partners
[[IMG:2]]
Sexual activity with other women
Note: Bacterial vaginosis is not an infection. It most commonly affects young women. Although it is not a sexually transmitted disease, the chances of developing bacterial vaginosis seem to increase with the number of sexual partners that a woman has had.

questions.stem: A young woman was suspected to have bacterial vaginosis. Which of the following statements is false about this condition?
options: Gardnerella vaginalis is a causative agent
Amsel’s criteria is used for diagnosis
Oral metronidazole is given for treatment
questions.explanation:
Vaginal itching is not seen in bacterial vaginosis. It is a symptom of Trichomonas vaginitis.
About half of the women having bacterial vaginosis are asymptomatic. Symptomatic women mostly present with a profuse, fishy vaginal discharge. It does not cause pruritus, dysuria, and dyspareunia.
Option A: Bacterial vaginosis occurs due to the absence of lactobacilli. This causes an increase in the growth of other anaerobic bacteria namely Gardnerella vaginalis, Mobiluncus, and Myco-plasma□ hominis.
Option B: Amsel's criteria is used for diagnosing bacterial vaginosis. 3 out of 4 criteria are needed to make a positive diagnosis.
Option D: Oral metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days or oral clindamycin 300 mg twice daily for 7 days is given for the treatment of bacterial vaginosis. Treatment remains the same in pregnancy.

questions.stem: A 30-year old woman presents to your OPD with complaints of foul-smelling vaginal discharge for the past 2 weeks. On examination, the discharge is adherent to the vaginal mucosa and has a fishy odour. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of bacterial vaginosis (BV) caused by Gardnerella.
Patients with BV have profuse and yellowish vaginal discharge with a fishy odour. It is adherent to the vaginal mucosa. Dysuria, dyspareunia, and vaginal itching are absent. On microscopy, clue cells are visible.
Option A: In trichomonas vaginitis, the vaginal discharge is frothy, greenish-yellow and has an offensive smell. Dysuria, dyspareunia, and vaginal itching are generally present.
Option B: In candidal vaginitis, the discharge is thick and curdy white.
Option D: In chlamydial infection, the vaginal discharge is generally scanty.

questions.stem: In a patient with bacterial vaginosis, which of the following microscopic features would not be seen?  [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]] [[IMG:3]]
questions.explanation:
An abundance of polymorphs is not a microscopic finding of bacterial vaginosis because it is not an inflammatory condition. It occurs due to an alteration in the normal vaginal flora.
A swab of the discharge is taken from the vaginal wall and a smear is prepared. The microscopic evaluation is done using a gram stained smear. In bacterial vaginosis, this would reveal a clean background with an abundance of gram variable coccobacilli adhering to the epithelial cells. These are called clue cells. A few inflammatory cells, other pathogenic organisms, and a reduced number of Lactobacilli would also be seen.
[[IMG:4]]
[[IMG:5]]
Shown below is the Gram-stained smear of vaginal discharge of a patient diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis. It reveals vaginal epithelial cells that have a fuzzy border due to the adherence of bacteria. These are called clue cells.

questions.stem: Given below is the image of a smear prepared from the vaginal discharge of a patient. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The presence of clue cells on microscopy is suggestive of bacterial vaginosis.
A swab of the vaginal discharge is taken from the vaginal wall and a smear is prepared. The microscopic evaluation of the smear is done on a gram stained smear. It would reveal a clean background with an abundance of gram variable coccobacilli adhering to the epithelial cells. These are called clue cells. A few inflammatory cells, other pathogenic organisms, and a reduced number of Lactobacilli would also be seen.
Shown below is the Gram-stained smear of vaginal discharge of a patient diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis. It reveals vaginal epithelial cells that have a fuzzy border due to the adherence of bacteria. These are called clue cells.

questions.stem: A woman comes to the clinic with complaints of foul-smelling vaginal discharge. On examination, the discharge was profuse and had a fishy odour. Which of the following is the best criteria to confirm the diagnosis? 700 Sold by @itachibot
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of bacterial vaginosis which is confirmed by using Amsel’s criteria.
3 out of 4 of the following criteria are needed, to make a positive diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis:
A homogeneous, thin, greyish-white discharge that smoothly coats the vaginal walls.
A vaginal pH > 4.5.
A positive whiff test - an amine like fishy odour is produced when a drop of 10% KOH is added to the sample of vaginal discharge.
The presence of >20% clue cells on saline wet mount. These are vaginal epithelial cells studded with adherent coccobacilli at the edge of the cell.
Option A: Boer-Miesel's criteria is used for the prognostic evaluation of pelvic inflammatory disease.
Option B: Light's criteria is used for determining the nature of the pleural fluid i.e., transudate or exudate, in the diagnosis of pleural effusion.
Option D: Nugent's criteria can also be used for diagnosing bacterial vaginosis. However, it is not the best confirmatory method.

questions.stem: In a patient with suspected bacterial vaginosis, Nugent's criteria is used to quantify the following bacteria except.... [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
Nugent's criteria is used to evaluate three types of bacteria in a case of suspected bacterial vaginosis: Mobiluncus, Lactobacillus, and Gardnerella/Bacteroides. Bacteria are graded through gram stain of vaginal samples.
They are each graded on a scale of 1+ to 4+ where:
1+ is < 1 cell per field
2+ is 1-5 cells per field
3+ is 6-30 cells per field
4+ is >30 cells per field
Lactobacillus and Bacteroides/Gardnerella are given scores between 0-4, but Mobiluncus is graded only from 0-2. The total scores are then calculated and interpreted as follows:
0-3 - Normal
4-6 - Intermediate bacterial count
[[IMG:2]]
[[IMG:3]]
7-10 - Bacterial vaginosis

questions.stem: A gynaecology resident noted a frothy, greenish, offensive-smelling vaginal discharge in a young lady. Whiff test was positive. Which organism is most likely implicated?
questions.explanation:
Trichomonas vaginalis is the likely organism implicated in this patient, causing trichomonas vaginitis.
The whiff test can be positive in both Trichomonas and Gardnerella infections. However, greenish frothy discharge is seen in trichomonas vaginitis.

questions.stem: A patient came to the gynaecology OPD with complaints of foul-smelling frothy vaginal discharge and intense itching. On examination, the cervix was spotted and had the appearance of a strawberry. Identify the causative organism.
questions.explanation:
In the given clinical scenario, Trichomonas vaginalis is the likely causative agent.
Vaginal itching and foul-smelling frothy vaginal discharge are seen in trichomonas vaginitis.
The given image shows colpitis macularis or strawberry cervix, which is a characteristic finding of trichomoniasis. This is due to microscopic, punctate haemorrhages of the cervix.

questions.stem: Which of the following organisms can be detected on a hanging drop preparation?
questions.explanation:
Trichomonas vaginalis can be detected on a hanging drop preparation. Trichomonas vaginalis is a protozoan with four anterior flagellae, and a fifth posterior flagellum responsible for motility.
The image given below shows trophozoites of Trichomonas vaginalis with flagella.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman came with complaints of greenish vaginal discharge. On saline microscopy, motile flagellated organisms were seen. What is the best treatment option for her? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:2]]
[[IMG:3]]
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of trichomonas vaginitis and the best treatment option for her is oral metronidazole 2 g stat.
The treatment regimen for trichomonas vaginitis is:
An oral dose of metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days or
A single oral dose of metronidazole 2 g
The male partner should be treated with a single dose of oral metronidazole in case of recurrent infection. Treatment in pregnancy remains the same.

questions.stem: A pregnant woman in her 7th week of gestation was diagnosed with trichomoniasis. Which of the following can be used to treat her condition?
questions.explanation:
Trichomonas vaginitis is treated with oral metronidazole in pregnant women.
According to the current guidelines, metronidazole is now considered safe for treating trichomonas vaginitis in pregnancy as it has no teratogenic effect.
The treatment regimen for trichomonas vaginitis in pregnant women include:
An oral dose of metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days or a single oral dose of metronidazole 2 g
Usage of trichofuran suppositories
Vinegar douche to lower the vaginal pH
Betadine gel
The male partner should be treated with a single dose of oral metronidazole in case of recurrent infection.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old diabetic woman presents to your OPD with complaints of curdy white vaginal discharge and intense itching. What is the likely causative agent for her condition?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of moniliasis and Candida albicans is the likely causative agent.
The risk factors for moniliasis are:
Diabetes mellitus
Obesity
Multiple sexual partners
Immunosuppression
HIV
Pregnancy
Steroid therapy
Following long-term broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy
Oral contraceptive pills
Poor personal hygiene.

questions.stem: In an obese lady with complaints of vaginal discharge, a vaginal pH of 4.2 was detected. Which organism is implicated in this patient?
questions.explanation:
The likely causative agent in the given clinical scenario is Candida which is known to flourish in an acidic environment. The pH of the vaginal discharge in candidal vaginitis is in the range of
4-4.5.

questions.stem: [[IMG:1]] Which of the following is not a risk factor for developing a candidal infection?
questions.explanation:
Hypertension does not increase the risk of developing a candidal infection. The risk factors for developing candidal vaginitis (moniliasis) are:
Diabetes mellitus
Obesity
Multiple sexual partners
Immunosuppression
HIV
Pregnancy
Steroid therapy
Following long-term broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy
Oral contraceptive pills
[[IMG:2]]
[[IMG:3]]
Poor personal hygiene.

questions.stem: A 32-year old woman presents to you with complaints of vaginal discharge and itching. On examination, you note a curdy white discharge and an inflamed vagina. What is the best treatment for her?
questions.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of candidal vaginitis. A single dose of fluconazole 150 mg is the best treatment for treating candidal vaginitis. Intravaginal antifungal (imidazole/miconazole/clotrimazole) vaginal pessaries or creams can also be used for 3–6 days.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a primary site for gonococcal infection?
questions.explanation:
Ectocervix and vagina are lined by squamous epithelium which is resistant to gonococcal infection.
The principal sites of invasion for gonococcal infection are the columnar and transitional epithelium. Hence, gonococcus usually affects the following structures:
Endocervix
Urethra
Skene’s glands
Bartholin's glands.

questions.stem: Which of the following presentations is unlikely to be seen in a patient with gonorrhoea? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
Haematuria is unlikely to be seen in a patient with gonorrhoea. Gynaecological presentation of gonorrhoea is:
Excessive vaginal discharge associated with pruritus and inflammation
[[IMG:2]]
Acute unilateral pain and swelling over labia due to the involvement of Bartholin’s gland
Intermenstrual bleeding
Non-gynaecological presentation of gonorrhoea is:
Pharyngeal infection
Dysuria
Rectal discomfort due to associated proctitis.

questions.stem: What is the most common cause of non-gonococcal urethritis?
questions.explanation:
The most common cause of non-gonococcal urethritis is Chlamydia trachomatis. The causes of non-gonococcal urethritis are:
Chlamydia trachomatis (most common)
Ureaplasma urealyticum
Adenovirus
Haemophillus vaginalis
Mycoplasma genitalium
Tricomonas vaginalis (rare)
Herpes simplex virus (rare)

questions.stem: A 35-year-old sex worker was suspected to have chlamydial cervicitis. What is the most sensitive method for confirming the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most sensitive method for confirming the diagnosis of chlamydial cervicitis is the polymerase chain reaction (PCR). It is fast, highly sensitive and specific (96%).

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman had complaints of lower abdominal pain and vaginal discharge. On microscopy, the following finding was present. What is the selective culture media used to isolate the causative organism? [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]]
options: Culture on bilayer human blood agar
questions.explanation:
Chlamydia trachomatis is the most likely causative organism. This is suggested by the presence of characteristic iodine-stained inclusion bodies in the McCoy cell culture of the patient's endocervical sample.
Chlamydia is a gram-negative coccobacillus. The gram stain of the cervical smear would show abundant leucocytes but no organisms.
The nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) is currently done for the diagnosis of lymphogranuloma venereum.

questions.stem: A patient with complaints of vaginal discharge was evaluated. On an endocervical biopsy, chlamydia was detected. How will you treat this patient?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
A single dose of 1 g of azithromycin is given and contact tracing is done to treat a patient diagnosed with a chlamydial infection.
Treatment of chlamydial infection:
Azithromycin 1 g single dose (or)
Doxycycline 100 mg orally BID × 7 days (or)
Ofloxacin 200 mg orally BID × 7 days (or)
Erythromycin 500 mg orally BID × 7 days
Contact tracing should always be done. The sexual partner should also be treated with the same regimen.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old lady complains of thick curdy white vaginal discharge with itching and burning. What is the route of administration of the first non-azole drug approved to treat this condition?
questions.explanation:
The clinical history of thick curdy white vaginal discharge with itching and burning are suggestive of vulvovaginal candidiasis. The first and the only non-azole antifungal approved for the treatment of vulvovaginal candidiasis is Ibrexafungerp. The route of administration of this drug is oral.
Ibrexafungerp is a triterpenoid antifungal agent that acts by inhibiting glucan synthase. Glucan synthase is an enzyme involved in the formation of 1,3-beta-D-glucan which is an essential component of the fungal cell wall.
The recommended dosage is 600 mg orally as 2 divided doses 12 hrs apart. Contraindications include pregnancy and hypersensitivity to ibrexafungerp. The most frequent adverse reactions are diarrhea, nausea, abdominal pain, dizziness, and vomiting.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the causative organism of vulval warts? [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]]
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:3]]
[[IMG:4]]
The causative agent of vulval warts is the human papillomavirus (HPV).
Genital warts/venereal warts/condyloma acuminata are verrucous growths that affect the skin of the labia majora, perineum, perianal region and vulva. The lesions may be discrete or coalesce to form cauliflower-like growth. The disease is sexually transmitted. The growth of the warts is favoured by vaginal discharge, the use of oral contraceptives, and pregnancy.
HPV causes structural changes in the epithelial cells of the skin called koilocytes, and their presence is characteristic of HPV infection. The koilocytes have large hyperchromatic nuclei and a perinuclear halo, as shown below.
The diagnosis is made by colposcopic studies. The lesions on the vulva are stained by toluidine blue. The abnormal areas of the skin retain the blue dye. These areas are then biopsied for histopathological examination.

questions.stem: A young woman presented with the following lesion on her vulva. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
The given image is suggestive of condyloma acuminata that shows cauliflower-like masses of tissue on and around the female anogenital region.
Condyloma acuminatum is an epidermal manifestation of the human papillomavirus (HPV).
HPV is transmitted through contact with infected skin or mucosa. The virus invades the cells of the epidermal basal layer through microabrasions. However, anogenital HPV infection is almost always acquired through sexual contact.
Warts are not required for transmission but are highly infectious because of their high viral load.
Option B: The image given below shows shiny, pearly white, umbilicated papules with a characteristic dimple at the centre. These are seen in molluscum contagiosum caused by the pox virus.
[[IMG:3]]
Option C: The image given below shows firm papules with a rough horny surface. These are seen in verruca vulgaris caused by the human papillomavirus type 2.

[[IMG:4]]
[[IMG:5]]
[[IMG:6]]
[[IMG:7]]
Option D: The image given below shows condyloma lata which is the characteristic feature of secondary syphilis. It is caused by Treponema pallidum.

questions.stem: A sexually active woman presents with cauliflower-like lesions on the vulva. The biopsy of the lesion is taken and histopathology reveals the following picture. What is the most likely causative organism? [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]]
questions.explanation:
The given image shows koilocytes, a characteristic feature of infection with human papillomavirus
(HPV).
Other features that can also be seen on histology are:
Perinuclear halo
723	Sold by @itachibot
Multinucleation
Orangeophilic cytoplasm
Acanthosis
Chronic inflammatory infiltrate
Option A: Henderson-Paterson bodies are seen in molluscum contagiosum, caused by poxvirus. Option C and D: Cowdry bodies are seen in herpes infection.

questions.stem: Which of the following serotypes are present in the bivalent vaccine against the human papillomavirus?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
Serotypes 16 and 18 are present in the bivalent vaccine against the human papillomavirus (HPV).
It is called Cervarix. Cervarix is given at 0, 1 and 6 months.
Gardasil/Silgard is the quadrivalent vaccine against HPV. It has serotypes 6, 11, 16 and 18 and is given at 0, 2 and 6 months.
Gardasil 9 is the nonavalent vaccine against HPV. It has serotypes 6, 11, 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52 and
58. In 2020 it has received an expanded indication which now includes the prevention of oropharyngeal and head and neck cancers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a treatment option for a patient with genital warts?
questions.explanation:
Genital warts are treated by a local application of 25% trichloracetic acid + 5% fluorouracil. Treatment of genital warts includes the local application of:
Podophyllin 25% in alcohol/podophyllin 20% in tincture benzoin daily for 4 days (or)
25% trichloracetic acid +5% fluorouracil daily for 4 days If this fails, the following treatment is given:
Interferon ointment/cream or intralesional interferon injection
Imiquimod cream thrice a week for 4 months
If medical treatment fails then cryosurgery, diathermy or laser removal is done.

questions.stem: A sexually active woman who presented with an ulcer over the vulva was diagnosed with primary syphilis. What is the characteristic feature associated with this condition? [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]]
options: Non suppurative, tender, and enlarged nodes
Firm, shotty, and painless nodes that do not suppurate
Painful, tender, and matted nodes forming an abscess
Painful, inflamed, necrotic nodes developing a chronic sinus
questions.explanation:
The characteristic feature associated with primary syphilis is firm, shotty, painless nodes that do not suppurate.
Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the motile spirochete, Treponema pallidum. In primary syphilis, the classical lesion i.e., chancre appears within 9–90 days from the first exposure.
The macular lesion becomes papular and then ulcerates. The ulcer(s) is painless and firm, with a punched out base and rolled edges. If left unattended, these heal within 3–9 weeks. It is accompanied by painless inguinal discrete lymphadenopathy.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman known to have syphilis presented with the following lesions over the vulva. What is the stage of the disease?
questions.explanation:
The given image shows condyloma lata, a classic finding of secondary syphilis.
Multiple moist well-demarcated papules and plaques are seen in condyloma lata. They are highly contagious, exophytic broad excrescences that ulcerate and are commonly seen on the vulva, perianal area and upper thighs.
[[IMG:1]]

questions.stem: A sexually active patient was diagnosed with lymphogranuloma venereum. What is the causative organism for this condition?
questions.explanation:
The causative agent for lymphogranuloma venereum is Chlamydia trachomatis (serotypes L1/L2/L3). Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is a sexually transmitted disease that causes genital ulcers.
It has the following three stages of infection:
Chlamydia trachomatis is a small gram-negative bacterium and an obligate intracellular parasite that appears as an intracytoplasmic inclusion body. The gram stain of the cervical smear would show leucocytes but no organisms. Hence, selective culture media like the McCoy cells culture is used to isolate the organism.
The slide given below is an iodine-stained smear prepared from the patient's endocervical sample. It shows inclusion bodies characteristic of Chlamydia trachomatis.

Primary stage | Painless genital ulcerPapules Lymphangitis
Secondary sta ge | Painful unilateral/bilateral ly mphadenopathyBuboesGroov e sign

questions.stem: [[IMG:1]] A 26-year-old sexually active man comes to the STD clinic with a painful genital ulcer. On examination, the ulcer and the right inguinal lymph nodes were tender. What is the causative organism?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:2]]
[[IMG:3]]
[[IMG:4]]
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of chancroid caused by Haemophilus ducreyi which is a gram-negative anaerobe.
Chancroid is symptomatic in men. Both ulcer and lymphadenopathy are
painful. Lymphadenopathy in chancroid is either unilateral or bilateral. Chancroid is generally asymptomatic in women but sometimes presents as painful lymphadenopathy.
The image below shows a chancroid ulcer with purulent and haemorrhagic discharge. It has a non-indurated, erythematous base.

questions.stem: A sexually active man presents with complaints of painful swelling over the inguinal region. He also gives a history of a painless genital ulcer that resolved spontaneously. On examination, groove sign is seen. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
[[IMG:3]]
The pathognomic groove sign of Greenblatt is suggestive of lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV)
caused by Chlamydia trachomatis (serovars L1, L2, L3).
This image shows groove sign which is seen in ■ of the cases in the secondary stage of LGV. It refers to the depression between the enlarged femoral and inguinal lymph nodes on either side of the inguinal ligament.
Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is a sexually transmitted disease that causes genital ulcers. It has the following three stages of infection:

questions.stem: A 20-year-old female sex worker presents with complaints of constipation and blood in stools for 3 months. On DRE, a circumferential constriction is felt beyond which the finger cannot be advanced. Which of the following is a probable cause for this complication?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of rectal stricture which is a complication of lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV).
LGV is a sexually transmitted disease caused by Chlamydia trachomatis (serotypes L1/L2/L3). Rectal involvement is commonly seen in women as the primary disease often goes unnoticed and untreated. Anorectal involvement causes proctocolitis and causes rectal strictures. This occurs due to the contiguous spread of the primary infection from the perirectal nodes leading to scar tissue formation.
The complications of lymphogranuloma venereum include:
Rectal stricture formation may lead to:
Intestinal obstruction
Rectovaginal fistulae
Proctitis
Vulvar cancer.

questions.stem: What is the causative agent for granuloma inguinale? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
The causative agent for granuloma inguinale (donovanosis) is Calymmatobacterium granulomatis. It is now called Klebsiella granulomatis and is a gram-negative bacillus causing chronic ulcerative infection of the vulva.
It is highly contagious and transmitted through repeated sexual or non-sexual contact. The incubation period is 1-12 weeks.
Clinical features:
It begins as a painless nodule which later ulcerates to form multiple beefy red painless ulcers that tend to coalesce; the vulva is progressively destroyed, and minimal adenopathy may occur.
Diagnosis:
Microscopic examination of smears from the lesion/ biopsy specimens reveals pathognomonic intracytoplasmic Donovan bodies and clusters of bacteria with a bipolar (safety pin) appearance.
Blue-black stained organisms are seen in the cytoplasm of mononuclear cells. Management:
Azithromycin 1 g orally once per week or 500 mg daily for at least 3 weeks and until all lesions have completely healed.
The given image below shows the donovanosis in a female patient with a beefy red ulcer:

questions.stem: A 19-year-old girl presented with multiple beefy-red ulcers over the labia. Microscopic examination of smear from the lesion showed intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies and gram-negative bacteria having a safety pin appearance. What is your likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
[[IMG:2]]
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of granuloma inguinale which is caused by a gram-negative bacteria, Klebsiella granulomatis.
Granuloma inguinale begins as a painless nodule that later ulcerates to form multiple beefy red painless ulcers. These ulcers tend to coalesce and bleed easily on contact. If secondarily infected, they may become painful. The ulcers heal by fibrosis, which can result in scarring resembling keloids.
The lymph nodes are usually uninvolved but can become enlarged. New lesions can appear along the lymphatic drainage channels.
The gross image below shows granuloma inguinale of the cervix with a beefy red appearance of the hypervascular intravaginal tissues.

[[IMG:3]]
[[IMG:4]]
[[IMG:5]]
[[IMG:6]]
The microscopic image below shows the pathognomonic intracytoplasmic Donovan bodies. It also shows clusters of gram-negative bacteria with a bipolar/safety-pin appearance.

questions.stem: The Pap smear of a healthy 30-year-old lady is given below. Identify the microorganism seen. [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]]
questions.explanation:
The organism seen in the given image of a Pap smear is the Doderlien’s bacillus, also known as Lactobacillus. This is a gram-positive, rod-shaped bacillus that grows in anaerobic conditions.
It is a part of the normal vaginal flora that is responsible for the vaginal defence mechanism. It is an estrogen-dependent bacillus and appears at puberty and disappears after menopause.
It converts glycogen into lactic acid and maintains the acidic ph in the vagina. This prevents the growth of pathogenic bacteria in the vagina. Its absence causes a condition called bacterial vaginosis where pathogenic organisms replaces the normal flora of the vagina. In this condition, clue cells are visible.
Option B: Gardnerella vaginalis is the most common organism involved in bacterial vaginosis. As the patient in the given question is healthy, this is not the correct option.
Option C: Trichomonas vaginalis is flagellated protozoa that causes trichomonas vaginitis. The organism and the nucleus of epithelial cells appear equal in size on the pap smear. This criterion is used for the identification of trichomonas as flagella are not visible on a pap smear.
Option D: Frisch bacillus is another name for Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis. It is not seen on Pap smears.

questions.stem: All of the following are risk factors for PID except .
questions.explanation:
Pregnancy is not a risk factor for PID. Instead, it plays a protective role in this condition.
The risk factors for developing PID are:
Unprotected sexual intercourse
Having multiple sex partners
Previous history of PID
IUD insertion
Early age of sexual intercourse (<18years)
The protective factors for PID are:
Pregnancy
[[IMG:1]]
Using barrier contraception like condoms, diaphragms
Oral contraceptive pills (OCPs)
Menopause

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is diagnosed with pelvic inflammatory disease. Which of the following is not included in this condition?
questions.explanation:
Cervicitis is not included in pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).
Pelvic inflammatory disease is a spectrum of infection and inflammation of the upper genital tract, typically causing:
Endometritis
Salpingitis
Oophoritis
Peritonitis
The minimum criteria for diagnosis of PID are:
Pain in the lower abdomen + any one of the following:
Uterine tenderness
Cervical motion tenderness
Adnexal tenderness
Cervicitis and vaginitis are lower genital tract infections.

questions.stem: [[IMG:1]] What is the most common symptom seen in acute PID?
options: Pain in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen
questions.explanation:
The most common symptom of acute PID is bilateral lower abdominal pain.
The pain is severe in acute stages and it may or may not be accompanied by a high temperature ( >38.3 degrees C). It may be followed by vomiting.
Some patients with PID can present with pain in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. This is seen in Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome which is a form of perihepatitis.
If PID occurs due to sexually transmitted organisms, dysuria and vaginal discharge may be seen.

questions.stem: A young woman with fever and lower abdominal pain is diagnosed to have PID. Which is the most common cause for this condition?
questions.explanation:
Chlamydia trachomatis is the most common cause of PID.
PID is an infection of the upper genital tract. It is generally transmitted sexually as an ascending infection along with sperms. It is usually a polymicrobial infection,
Organisms causing PID include:
[[IMG:1]]
Sexually transmitted:
Chlamydia (most common)
Gonococcus
Mycoplasma
Trichomonas Pyogenic Aerobes:
Staphylococci
Streptococci
E Coli Anaerobes:
Bacteroides fragilis
Peptostreptococcus
Clostridium
Actinomyces (most common in IUD users) Other:
Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Note: Genital tuberculosis is the only PID that does not spread sexually. It has a hematogenous spread. Thus, it is the most common PID in virgin girls.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman presented to the emergency room with abdominal pain and fever for the last 48 hours. She has been using a Cu T 380A for contraception for the past 8 years. On examination, cervical motion tenderness was present. What is the most likely organism to have caused her condition?
questions.explanation:
The given clinical scenario points towards a diagnosis of PID in an IUCD user. The most common organism causing this condition is Actinomyces. It has been reported in 7% of IUCD users if the device is worn for more than 2 years.
This emphasizes the need for strict asepsis during insertion of the device and the need for strict follow up of women wearing these devices.
Organisms causing PID are:

questions.stem: What is the mechanism of the spread of gonococci to the tubes in pelvic inflammatory disease? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
The mechanism of the spread of gonococci to the tubes in pelvic inflammatory disease is mucosal.
Gonococci ascend to the tubes mainly through mucosal continuity. This is facilitated by sexually transmitted vectors such as sperms and Trichomonas.
The mucous membranes of the fallopian tubes are affected first. They become edematous and are infiltrated with leukocytes and plasma cells. Another route of spread is through the reflux of mucosal blood.
Option A: Hematogenous spread is seen in genital tuberculosis.
Option B: Lymphatics are involved in the spread of secondary organisms and in PID following post-abortal and puerperal infection.
Option C: Parametrium facilitates the spread of Mycoplasma. The gut flora can directly spread to tubes.

questions.stem: Which infection causes more damage to the mucosa and the wall of the tube leading to fibrosis and tubal blockage?
questions.explanation:
Among the given options, chlamydial infection causes the most amount of damage to the mucosa and the wall of the fallopian tubes leading to fibrosis and tubal blockage.
Chlamydial infection can remain asymptomatic in the endo-cervix. Hence, the infection goes unnoticed and untreated. Thus, it can lead to more damage and complications.
Gonococcal infection is more symptomatic than chlamydial infection. Hence, it is diagnosed early and causes less damage to the tubes than chlamydial infection.
Mycoplasma and Mobiluncus generally cause lower genital tract infections like cervicitis and vaginitis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a differential diagnosis of acute PID?
questions.explanation:
[[IMG:1]]
Pelvic endometriosis is not a differential diagnosis of acute PID. It is a differential diagnosis of chronic PID.
Differential diagnosis of acute PID:
Acute appendicitis
Septic abortion
Cholecystitis
Twisted ovarian cyst
Ectopic pregnancy
Diverticulitis
Ruptured endometriotic cyst Differential diagnosis of chronic PID:
Uterine fibroids
Pelvic endometriosis
Ovarian tumour
Tubercular tubo-ovarian mass

questions.stem: A 26-year-old female with endometritis did not complete the course of antibiotics she was prescribed. Following this, her infection failed to resolve and she developed a tubo-ovarian mass. How can this mass manifest?
questions.explanation:
The given scenario of development of a chronic tubo-ovarian mass following acute PID points towards a diagnosis of chronic PID. A chronic tubo-ovarian mass can manifest as a tubo-ovarian cyst, hydrosalpinx or even a chronic pyosalpinx.
Failure to complete treatment of acute PID or drug resistance can lead to the development of chronic PID. This can lead to the development of chronic tubo-ovarian masses which may manifest as:
Hydrosalpinx
Chronic pyosalpinx
Chronic interstitial salpingitis
Tubo-ovarian cyst
Tuberculous form
A twisted ovarian cyst and a ruptured endometriotic cyst are differential diagnoses of acute PID.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the condition seen in the image given below? [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]]
options: Flattening of tubal plicae is seen on histology
Its ampullary region is filled with clear fluid
questions.explanation:
The above image depicts a hydrosalpinx. Its wall is not opaque but translucent.
If a pyosalpinx responds to antibiotics, the pus present inside becomes sterile within 6 weeks of the initial attack. However, the damage to the tube remains as chronic pyosalpinx or hydrosalpinx. A hydrosalpinx represents the end result of previous acute salpingitis and is often bilateral.
[[IMG:3]]
The tube becomes retort shaped due to the enormous dilatation of the ampullary region that is filled with clear fluid.
Histological examination shows a flattening of the tubal plicae and exfoliation of the lining epithelium.

questions.stem: A patient with fever and abdominal pain presented to the emergency. On examination, you note mucopurulent vaginal discharge and cervical motion tenderness. You suspect she has PID. Which of these is not included in the criteria to diagnose this condition?
questions.explanation:
Bilateral abdominal pain is not included in the criteria to diagnose PID. Bilateral abdominal pain is a clinical symptom of PID.
Lower abdominal tenderness is included in the criteria to diagnose PID. CDC criteria for the diagnosis of PID:
Definitive criteria:
Histopathologic evidence of endometritis on biopsy
Imaging study (TVS/MRI) evidence of thickened fluid-filled tubes (tubo-ovarian abscess)
Laparoscopic evidence of PID Minimum criteria:
Cervical motion tenderness
Uterine tenderness
Adnexal tenderness Additional criteria:
Oral temperature >38.3 oC
Mucopurulent cervical or vaginal discharge, cervical friability
Raised ESR or CRP
Laboratory documentation of positive cervical infection with Gonorrhea or Chlamydia

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a definitive criterion used to diagnose PID? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
A temperature of more than 38.3°C is an additional criterion and not a definitive criterion for the diagnosis of PID.
CDC 2006 criteria for the diagnosis of PID:
Definitive criteria:
Histopathologic evidence of endometritis on biopsy
[[IMG:2]]
Imaging studies (TVS/MRI) evidence of thickened fluid-filled tubes (Tubo-ovarian abscess)

Lower abdominal tenderness

Oral temperature>38.3C

Laboratory documentation of positive cervical infection with Gonorrhea or Chlamydia

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman presented with bilateral abdominal pain for 3 days and a temperature of 102°F. She also had a mucopurulent vaginal discharge, cervical motion tenderness, and a negative urine pregnancy test. Which is the gold standard investigation to confirm her likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The given clinical scenario is likely to be acute PID. Laparoscopy is the gold standard to confirm acute PID.
Laparoscopy is not done routinely as it is an invasive procedure. It is reserved for only cases where the differential diagnosis is salpingitis, appendicitis, ectopic pregnancy or a case of a non-responding pelvic mass.
The diagnosis of PID is mostly clinical. If diagnosis is unclear, the investigation of choice for PID is USG and culdocentesis.
CDC 2006 criteria for the diagnosis of PID:
Definitive criteria:
Histopathologic evidence of endometritis on biopsy
Imaging studies (TVS/MRI) evidence of thickened fluid-filled tubes (tubo-ovarian abscess)
Laparoscopic evidence of PID Minimum criteria:
Lower abdominal tenderness
Adnexal tenderness
Cervical motion tenderness Additional criteria:
Oral temperature>38.3C
Mucopurulent cervical or vaginal discharge and cervical friability
Raised ESR or CRP
Laboratory documentation of positive cervical infection with Gonorrhea or Chlamydia

questions.stem: The laparoscopy report of a woman with pelvic inflammatory disease states she has Gainesville stage III PID. Which of the following presentations could have been seen in her?
questions.explanation:
Gainesville stage III includes two forms of PID - acute salpingitis with superimposed tubal occlusion or tubo-ovarian complex.
Gainesville has described the stages of PID depending upon the severity of tubal damage as follows:
Stage | Condition
Stage I | Acute salpingitis without peri tonitis - no adhesions
Stage I I | Acute salpingitis with periton itis - purulent discharge
Stage I II | Acute salpingitis with superi mposed tubal occlusion or tu bo-ovarian complex
Stage I V | Ruptured tubo-ovarian absce ss
Stage V | Tubercular salpingitis

questions.stem: In a patient with PID, laparoscopy shows the following appearance. What is true about the syndrome this patient likely has? [[IMG:1]] [[IMG:2]]
questions.explanation:
The image shows the laparoscopic finding of violin string adhesions that are characteristic of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome. It is a form of perihepatitis that occurs in the setting of PID.
It is characterized by right upper quadrant pain with a pleuritic component, sometimes referred to the right shoulder. It rarely occurs in women with acute PID. The pathological mechanism is as follows:
Gonococcal / Chlamydial infection  transperitoneal/vascular spread  inflammation of the liver capsule and peritoneal surfaces  adhesions and fibrosis in the perihepatic region 
Fitz-Hugh-Curtis Syndrome
Cholecystitis and ruptured tubo-ovarian abscess are the differential diagnoses of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome. Violin string adhesions would not be seen in these conditions.

questions.stem: Identify the wrong statement with respect to silent PID.
options: Mycobacterium can be grown from menstrual blood
questions.explanation:
Dysmenorrhea rarely occurs in PID. Pain is uncommon and is a result of subacute PID.
Silent PID is thought to follow multiple or continuous low-grade infections in asymptomatic women. It is not a clinical diagnosis. Rather, it is an ultimate diagnosis given to women with tubal-factor infertility who lack a history of upper genital tract infection.
[[IMG:1]]
On laparoscopy or laparotomy, these women may have evidence of prior tubal infection such as adhesions, but for the most part, the fallopian tubes are grossly normal. They can have ectopic pregnancies due to tubal dysmotility. Silent PID can occur following infection with M. tuberculosis.

questions.stem: A patient is admitted to the gynaecology ward for pelvic inflammatory disease. Which of the following is a part of this patient's treatment regimen?
options: Administration of cefotetan 2 g IV 12 hourly + doxycycline 100 mg IV BD
Removal of IUD irrespective of antibiotic response
Administration of a single dose of ceftriaxone 250 mg IM
Administration of 10 doses of Placentrex 2ml IM daily or on alternate days
questions.explanation:
Administration of cefotetan 2 g IV 12hourly + doxycycline 100 mg BD orally/ IV for 48 hours forms the crux of the treatment regimen for PID. This is followed by oral doxycycline 100 mg
+/-metronidazole 400 mg for 14 days in all hospitalized patients having PID. Treatment of PID in hospitalized patients:
Cefotetan 2 g IV 12hourly + doxycycline 100 mg BD orally/ IV for 48 hours is given followed by oral doxycycline 100 mg +/- metronidazole 400 mg for 14 days
Cefoxitin 2 g IV 6hourly + doxycycline 100 mg IV followed by oral route.
Azithromycin 500 mg IV 6 hourly for 2 days, then orally for Chlamydia. Outpatient treatment of PID (according to the current RCOG guidelines):
A single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg followed by oral doxycycline 100 mg BD +/-
metronidazole 400 mg BD x 14 days
A single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg followed by azithromycin 1 gm per week x 2 weeks.
IUD is not removed in a woman who responds to antibiotics. It is removed only in case of a failed antibiotic response. Barrier contraceptives and OCPs are recommended only in women unresponsive to antibiotics.
The use of Placentrex (aqueous extract of the placenta) is outdated and is not recommended currently.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old female presents to the OPD with fever, lower abdominal pain and purulent vaginal discharge. On examination, her vitals are stable and per vaginal examination reveals lower abdominal and cervical motion tenderness. What is the best treatment option for her? [[IMG:1]]
options: Single IM injection of ceftriaxone 250 mg with oral doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days
Single IM injection of ceftriaxone 250 mg with oral metronidazole 400 mg for 7 days
Oral doxycycline 100 mg BD with oral metronidazole 400 mg for 7 days
Oral ofloxacin 200 mg BD with oral metronidazole 400 mg for 14 days
questions.explanation:
The given clinical scenario of fever and lower abdominal pain associated with lower abdominal and cervical motion tenderness is suggestive of PID. The best treatment option for this patient is
outpatient treatment with a single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg + oral doxycycline 100 mg BD
+/- metronidazole 400 mg BD x 14 days.
Outpatient treatment of PID (according to the current RCOG guidelines):
A single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg + oral doxycycline 100 mg BD +/- metronidazole 400 mg BD x 14 days
A single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg followed by azithromycin 1 gm per week x 2 weeks. Treatment of PID in hospitalized patients:
Cefotetan 2 g IV 12hourly + doxycycline 100 mg BD orally/ IV for 48 hours is given followed by oral doxycycline 100 mg +/- metronidazole 400 mg for 14 days
[[IMG:2]]

questions.stem: Which of the following would be an indication for surgery in a 30-year-old woman diagnosed with PID?
questions.explanation:
Intestinal obstruction would be an indication for surgery in a patient diagnosed with PID. Criteria for surgery in PID include:
Drainage of pelvic abscess by colpotomy.
Dilatation and evacuation of septic products of conception or for haemorrhage in the postabortal period.
Acute spreading peritonitis resistant to a full course of chemotherapy. Presence of pyoperitoneum mandates laparotomy.
Intestinal obstruction
Suspected intestinal injury as diagnosed in criminal abortion.
Ruptured tubo-ovarian abscess
A tubo-ovarian abscess of 2 cm is not an indication for surgery. Minimally invasive surgery is done in a tubo-ovarian abscess measuring more than 10 cm, that fails to respond to antibiotics in 48-72 hours.
Peritonitis and sepsis are not an indication for surgery. They should be managed medically first. If they do not respond to antibiotic treatment then surgical management should be done.

questions.stem: Which among the following is an indication for minimally invasive surgery for tubo-ovarian abscess?
options: The size of the abscess is more than 5 cm
The size of the abscess is more than 2cm
The abscess fails to respond to antibiotics in 48 - 72 h
The abscess fails to respond to antibiotics in 24 - 36 h
questions.explanation:
If the abscess fails to respond to antibiotics in 48–72 h, minimally invasive surgery is indicated. Criteria for minimally invasive surgery in PID:
The size of the abscess is more than 10 cm
The abscess fails to respond to antibiotics in 48-72 hours
The abscess ruptures
Pyoperitoneum
Minimal invasive surgery includes laparoscopic drainage of the tubo ovarian abscess or posterior colpotomy.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old multiparous woman who presented with chronic lower abdominal pain has been diagnosed with chronic PID. What is the treatment of choice for this patient?
questions.explanation:
The treatment of choice for an old multiparous woman with chronic PID is abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy.
[[IMG:1]]
A radical hysterectomy involves the removal of the whole uterus, tissue from the sides of the uterus, the cervix, and the upper part of the vagina. It is generally done only in cancer patients.
A supracervical hysterectomy involves the removal of only the body of the uterus and is not done in chronic PID. It is done for the treatment of endometriosis, uterine fibroids, and uterine prolapse.

questions.stem: Who has described the prognostic evaluation for PID? [[IMG:1]]
questions.explanation:
Boer-Meisel has described the prognostic evaluation for PID. It depends upon the following:
Extent of adhesions
Nature of adhesions such as flimsy or dense.
Size of hydrosalpinx
Macroscopic condition of hydrosalpinx.
The thickness of the tubal wall.
Boer-Meisel system is specifically used for predicting pregnancy outcomes in patients treated for PID.
Gainesville has described the stages of PID depending upon the severity of tubal damage.
Westrom has reported that women with one previous attack of PID have a predisposition to another attack.
 | Stages of PID
Stage I | Acute salpingitis without peri tonitis - no adhesions
Stage I I | Acute salpingitis with periton itis- purulent discharge
Stage I II | Acute salpingitis with superi mposed tubal occlusion or tu bo-ovarian complex
Stages of PID | Stages of PID
Stage I V | Ruptured tubo-ovarian absce ss
Stage V | Tuberculous salpingitis

questions.stem: Long-standing pelvic inflammation may lead to which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
Long-standing pelvic inflammation may lead to pyometra. This refers to the collection of pus in the uterine cavity.
[[IMG:1]]
The initial infection involves the cervix uteri and urethra which may extend to Bartholin glands, skene glands, endometrium, and fallopian tubes. Unilateral pain and swelling over the labia may be caused by the inflammation of the Bartholin glands.
Depending on the extent of tissue involved, PID can be classified into five stages
Stage I - Acute salpingitis without peritonitis - No adhesions
Stage II - Acute salpingitis with peritonitis - purulent discharge
Stage III - Acute salpingitis with superimposed tubal occlusion or tubo ovarian complex
Stage IV - Ruptured tubo-ovarian abscess
Stage V - Tubercular salpingitis
Long-standing pelvic inflammation may also lead to:
Dyspareunia
Infertility
Ectopic pregnancy
Formation of adhesions like hydrosalpinx, pyosalpinx, tubo-ovarian abscess
Chronic pelvic pain
Note: Chronic pelvic inflammation leads to dense adhesions between the uterus and the appendages. Thus, it becomes difficult to define the uterus from the pelvic masses. They form a hard mass which is called the frozen pelvis.
The most common cause of the spread of PID: Ascending infection along with sperms
The only PID that does not spread with the sexual route is genital TB. It has a hematogenous spread.
The most common PID in virgin females is genital TB. Investigation of choice in PID: Abdominal USG
The surest sign of salpingitis is pus extruding from the fimbrial end of the tube.

questions.explanation:
